Second conditional: If I were….explain_en: We use the second conditional for situations that are imaginary or unlikely now or in the future: “If I had a million dollars, I would travel the world.”
Second conditional: If I were….explain_ar: بنستخدم الشرط التاني لمواقف خيالية أو بعيدة دلوقتي أو في المستقبل: “If I had a million dollars, I would travel the world.”

examples.en: If I lived by the sea, I would swim every day.
examples.ar: لو كنت ساكن جنب البحر كنت هعوم كل يوم.

examples.en: What would you do if you won the lottery?
examples.ar: كنت هتعمل إيه لو كسبت اليانصيب؟

check.question: Which sentence is imaginary?
options: If it rains, I’ll stay home.
If I were a bird, I would fly.
If you heat ice, it melts.
check.why_ar: إني أبقى طير حاجة خيالية → الشرط التاني.

Second conditional: If I were….explain_en: Use if + past simple, then would + base verb. The past form here does not mean past time — it shows the situation is not real.
Second conditional: If I were….explain_ar: if + ماضي بسيط، وبعدين would + الفعل في أصله. الماضي هنا مش معناه زمن فات، معناه إن الموقف مش حقيقي.

examples.en: If she studied more, she would get better marks.
examples.ar: لو كانت بتذاكر أكتر كانت هتجيب درجات أحسن.

examples.en: I would buy that car if it were cheaper.
examples.ar: كنت هشتري العربية دي لو كانت أرخص.

check.question: If I ___ more time, I would learn Spanish.
check.why_ar: بعد if في الشرط التاني بنستخدم الماضي: had.

Second conditional: If I were….explain_en: With “be”, we often use “were” for everyone: “If I were rich…”, “If she were here…”. “If I were you, I would…” is a polite way to give advice.
Second conditional: If I were….explain_ar: مع be بنستخدم were مع الكل: “If I were rich”. و“If I were you, I would…” طريقة مؤدبة للنصيحة.
Second conditional: If I were….board: If I were you, I would …

examples.en: If I were you, I would take the job.
examples.ar: لو كنت مكانك كنت قبلت الشغلانة.

examples.en: If he were taller, he could play basketball.
examples.ar: لو كان أطول كان يقدر يلعب باسكت.

check.question: Choose the best advice:
options: If I am you, I will rest.
If I were you, I would rest.
If I was you, I rest.
check.why_ar: للنصيحة بنقول If I were you, I would.

Second conditional: If I were….explain_en: Real and possible → first conditional (if + present, will). Imaginary or very unlikely → second (if + past, would). Compare: “If I see him, I’ll tell him” / “If I saw a lion, I’d run.”
Second conditional: If I were….explain_ar: لو ممكن يحصل فعلاً → الشرط الأول. لو خيالي أو بعيد جداً → الشرط التاني.
Second conditional: If I were….board: possible → if + present, will · imaginary → if + past, would

examples.en: If I pass the exam, I’ll celebrate. (possible)
If I could fly, I’d visit every country. (imaginary)
examples.ar: لو أقدر أطير كنت زرت كل البلاد. (خيال)

check.question: “If I ___ the president, I would build more schools.”
check.why_ar: موقف خيالي → were.

Second conditional: If I were….recap_en: Use if + past simple with would + verb for imaginary or unlikely situations, use were for everyone, and say “If I were you” to give advice.

The passive: It was made….explain_en: We use the passive when the action is more important than who did it, or when we don’t know who did it: “My phone was stolen.”
The passive: It was made….explain_ar: بنستخدم المبني للمجهول لما الفعل يكون أهم من اللي عمله، أو لما مانكونش عارفين مين عمله: “My phone was stolen.”
The passive: It was made….board: the action matters, not who did it

examples.en: This bridge was built in 1990.
Arabic is spoken in many countries.

check.question: Which sentence is passive?
options: They clean the room every day.
The room is cleaned every day.
check.why_ar: the room is cleaned = الأوضة بتتنضف (مبني للمجهول).

The passive: It was made….explain_en: Make the passive with the verb “be” in the right tense + the past participle: is made, was made, has been made, will be made.
The passive: It was made….explain_ar: المبني للمجهول = be في الزمن المناسب + التصريف التالت: is made وwas made وwill be made.
The passive: It was made….board:
present: is / are + done
past: was / were + done

examples.en: Cars are made in this factory.
The letters were sent yesterday.

check.question: The pyramids ___ thousands of years ago.
check.why_ar: في الماضي ومجهول: were built.

The passive: It was made….explain_en: If we want to say who did the action, we use “by”: “The Mona Lisa was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.” Often we leave it out because it isn’t important.
The passive: It was made….explain_ar: لو عايزين نقول مين عمل الفعل بنستخدم by: “… was painted by Leonardo da Vinci.” وغالباً بنشيله لو مش مهم.

examples.en: The book was written by Naguib Mahfouz.
The match was watched by millions.

check.question: The phone was invented ___ Alexander Graham Bell.
check.why_ar: اللي عمل الفعل بييجي بعد by.

The passive: It was made….explain_en: Don’t forget “be”: “The car was repaired”, not “The car repaired”. And the verb must be the past participle: “It was written”, not “It was wrote”.
The passive: It was made….explain_ar: ماتنساش be: “The car was repaired” مش “The car repaired”. والفعل لازم تصريف تالت: written مش wrote.

examples.en: The windows are cleaned every week.
Dinner will be served at 8.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
check.why_ar: لازم was + التصريف التالت sent.

The passive: It was made….recap_en: The passive is be + past participle. We use it when the action matters more than the doer, and add by only when we want to say who did it.

Reported speech: She said that….explain_en: We use reported speech to tell someone what another person said, without their exact words: “I’m tired.” → She said (that) she was tired.
Reported speech: She said that….explain_ar: بنستخدم الكلام المنقول عشان نحكي اللي حد قاله من غير كلامه بالحرف: She said (that) she was tired.
Reported speech: She said that….board: direct: “I’m tired.” → reported: She said she was tired.

examples.en: He said he liked the film.
They said they were hungry.

check.question: Which is reported speech?
check.why_ar: من غير علامات تنصيص ومع تغيير الزمن → كلام منقول.

Reported speech: She said that….explain_en: After “said”, we usually move the tense one step back: am/is → was, present simple → past simple, will → would, can → could.
Reported speech: She said that….explain_ar: بعد said بنرجّع الزمن خطوة لورا: am → was، والمضارع → ماضي، وwill → would، وcan → could.
Reported speech: She said that….board: is → was · like → liked · will → would · can → could

examples.en: “I will help you.” → He said he would help me.
“I can swim.” → She said she could swim.

check.question: “I live in Cairo.” → He said he ___ in Cairo.
check.why_ar: المضارع بيرجع ماضي: lived.

Reported speech: She said that….explain_en: Change pronouns and time words to match: I → he/she, my → his/her, today → that day, tomorrow → the next day, here → there.
Reported speech: She said that….explain_ar: غيّر الضماير وكلمات الوقت: I → he/she، وtomorrow → the next day، وhere → there.
Reported speech: She said that….board: tomorrow → the next day · here → there

examples.en: “I’ll see you tomorrow.” → She said she would see me the next day.
“My car is here.” → He said his car was there.

check.question: “I’m busy today.” → She said she was busy ___.
check.why_ar: today بتبقى that day في الكلام المنقول.

Reported speech: She said that….explain_en: “Tell” needs a person: “He told me…”; “say” doesn’t: “He said…”. Reported questions use normal word order: “Where do you live?” → She asked where I lived.
Reported speech: She said that….explain_ar: tell لازم بعدها شخص: “He told me”. وsay لأ: “He said”. والسؤال المنقول ترتيبه زي الجملة العادية: She asked where I lived.
Reported speech: She said that….board: tell + person · say (no person) · asked where I lived

examples.en: She told me she was leaving.
He asked if I was ready.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
check.why_ar: مع الشخص بنستخدم told me.

Reported speech: She said that….recap_en: In reported speech we move tenses one step back, change pronouns and time words, use tell with a person, and keep normal word order in questions.

used to / be used to.explain_en: Use “used to + verb” for habits or states in the past that are not true now: “I used to play football every day.” (Now I don’t.)
used to / be used to.explain_ar: used to + الفعل لعادات أو أحوال في الماضي ما بقتش موجودة: “I used to play football every day.”

examples.en: We used to live in Tanta.
She used to have long hair.

check.question: Which means “زمان كنت بخاف من الكلاب”?
options: I used to be afraid of dogs.
I am used to be afraid of dogs.
I use to afraid of dogs.
check.why_ar: عادة أو حالة في الماضي → used to + الفعل.

used to / be used to.explain_en: Negative: “didn’t use to” (no -d). Question: “Did you use to…?”: “I didn’t use to like vegetables.” “Did you use to walk to school?”
used to / be used to.explain_ar: النفي: didn’t use to (من غير d). والسؤال: Did you use to…?
used to / be used to.board: didn’t use to · Did you use to …?

examples.en: He didn’t use to wear glasses.
Did you use to watch cartoons?

check.question: I ___ like coffee, but now I love it.
check.why_ar: بعد didn’t بنكتب use من غير d.

used to / be used to.explain_en: “Be used to + noun or -ing” means something is normal or familiar for you now: “I’m used to the hot weather.” “She’s used to getting up early.”
used to / be used to.explain_ar: be used to + اسم أو ing معناها متعود على حاجة دلوقتي: “I’m used to the hot weather.”
used to / be used to.board: be used to + noun / -ing = متعود على

examples.en: I’m used to living alone.
He isn’t used to the noise yet.
examples.ar: هو لسه مش متعود على الدوشة.

check.question: She ___ driving on the right now.
check.why_ar: متعودة على حاجة دلوقتي → is used to + ing.

used to / be used to.explain_en: “Get used to” describes the process of becoming familiar: “It took me a month to get used to my new school.”
used to / be used to.explain_ar: get used to = بدأت أتعود، عملية التعود نفسها: “It took me a month to get used to my new school.”

examples.en: You’ll soon get used to the food here.
I’m getting used to working from home.
examples.ar: ببدأ أتعود على الشغل من البيت.

check.question: Choose the correct sentence:
options: I can’t get used to wake up early.
I can’t get used to waking up early.
I can’t get use to wake up early.
check.why_ar: بعد get used to بنستخدم ing.

used to / be used to.recap_en: Used to + verb is for past habits. Be used to + noun or -ing means something is familiar now, and get used to is the process of becoming familiar.

Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.explain_en: When one verb follows another, the second verb is either -ing (a gerund) or to + verb (an infinitive). It depends on the first verb.
Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.explain_ar: لما فعل ييجي بعد فعل، التاني يا إما ing يا إما to + فعل، وده حسب الفعل الأول.

examples.en: I enjoy reading.
I want to read.

check.question: Which is correct?
check.why_ar: want بييجي بعدها to + فعل.

Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.explain_en: Use -ing after enjoy, finish, mind, avoid, keep, suggest, can’t stand: “I finished doing my homework.” Also after prepositions: “good at drawing”.
Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.explain_ar: ing بعد enjoy وfinish وmind وavoid وkeep وsuggest، وبعد حروف الجر: good at drawing.

examples.en: Would you mind closing the door?
She’s interested in learning Japanese.

check.question: Have you finished ___ the book?
check.why_ar: بعد finish بنستخدم ing.

Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.explain_en: Use to + verb after want, decide, hope, plan, need, learn, promise, would like: “We decided to stay.” “I’d like to order, please.”
Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.explain_ar: to + فعل بعد want وdecide وhope وplan وneed وlearn وpromise وwould like.
Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.board: want / decide / hope / need + to + verb

examples.en: He promised to call me.
I need to buy some bread.

check.question: They hope ___ the competition.
check.why_ar: بعد hope بنستخدم to + الفعل.

Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.explain_en: A few verbs take both with different meanings: “I stopped smoking” (I don’t smoke now) vs “I stopped to drink water” (I stopped in order to drink). “Remember to lock the door” (don’t forget) vs “I remember locking it” (I have a memory of it).
Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.explain_ar: أفعال قليلة بتاخد الاتنين بمعنى مختلف: stopped smoking (بطّلت) وstopped to drink (وقفت عشان أشرب). remember to (ماتنساش) وremember doing (فاكر إني عملت).
Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.board: stop doing ≠ stop to do · remember to do ≠ remember doing

examples.en: Please remember to bring your book.
I remember meeting her at the party.

check.question: He stopped ___ to answer the phone. (He paused his work.)
check.why_ar: وقف الشغل نفسه → stopped working.

Gerund or infinitive: enjoy doing / want.recap_en: Some verbs like enjoy and finish take -ing, others like want and decide take to + verb, and a few like stop and remember change meaning.

Phrasal verbs for everyday life.explain_en: A phrasal verb is a verb + a small word like up, off, on or out. Together they have a new meaning: “get up” means to leave your bed.
Phrasal verbs for everyday life.explain_ar: الفعل المركب هو فعل + كلمة صغيرة زي up أو off أو on أو out، ومع بعض بيدوا معنى جديد: get up = تقوم من السرير.
Phrasal verbs for everyday life.board: verb + up / off / on / out = new meaning

examples.en: I get up at 6 every day.
Turn off the light, please.

check.question: “Get up” means …
check.why_ar: get up = تقوم من السرير.

Phrasal verbs for everyday life.explain_en: Many common actions use phrasal verbs: wake up, get dressed, put on (clothes), take off (clothes), turn on / turn off, go out.
Phrasal verbs for everyday life.explain_ar: أفعال يومية كتير مركبة: wake up وput on (تلبس) وtake off (تقلع) وturn on / off وgo out.
Phrasal verbs for everyday life.board: put on ≠ take off · turn on ≠ turn off

examples.en: Put on your jacket — it’s cold.
We’re going out for dinner tonight.

check.question: It’s hot. ___ your coat.
check.why_ar: لما الجو حر بنقلع: take off.

Phrasal verbs for everyday life.explain_en: With many phrasal verbs, the object can go in the middle: “turn the TV off” or “turn off the TV”. But with a pronoun (it, them), it must go in the middle: “turn it off”, not “turn off it”.
Phrasal verbs for everyday life.explain_ar: أفعال مركبة كتير بنحط المفعول في النص أو في الآخر. لكن مع الضمير (it أو them) لازم في النص: “turn it off” مش “turn off it”.
Phrasal verbs for everyday life.board: turn it off ✓ · turn off it ✗

examples.en: Pick up your toys. — Pick them up!
Can you fill in this form? — Fill it in, please.

check.question: Your music is loud. Please turn ___.
check.why_ar: مع it بنحطها في النص: turn it down.

Phrasal verbs for everyday life.explain_en: Learn them in real sentences: look for (search), find out (discover), give up (stop trying), look after (take care of), run out of (have no more).
Phrasal verbs for everyday life.explain_ar: اتعلمهم في جمل حقيقية: look for (يدوّر)، find out (يعرف)، give up (يستسلم)، look after (ياخد باله من)، run out of (يخلص منه).
Phrasal verbs for everyday life.board: look for · find out · give up · look after · run out of

examples.en: I’m looking for my keys.
We’ve run out of milk.

check.question: Don’t ___ ! You can do it!
check.why_ar: give up = تستسلم.

Phrasal verbs for everyday life.recap_en: Phrasal verbs are a verb plus a small word with a new meaning. Learn them in real sentences, and put pronouns like it in the middle.
